text:
leila: Heads-up — I saw recurring p95 spikes (~250ms -> 420ms) on route `search/gen-1` during the 11:30 load test. Traces point to batch formation + kernel switchover overhead + KV-cache churn. Putting log snippet in /perf/traces/3098765432 :eyes:

kevin: ugh. can you paste the perf counters? is it microbatching waiting longer or kernel switch penalty when batch reaches X tokens?

leila: paste from flame: `microbatch_wait_ms` increases sharply when `batch_tokens` crosses ~1200 and we hit a different kernel path. KV hit-rate drops from 92% -> 68% at the same time (lots of prefix diversity).

sasha: interesting — that smells like two interacting heuristics. If batcher tries to maximize token fill across heterogeneous routes, it mixes prefixes and kills KV locality. propose: make dynamic token-budget per route/tier enforceable during formation (prefer homogeneous slices).

maria: agreed. short plan: 1) add per-route moving-average p95 target, 2) when forming batches, score candidate requests by (route, kv_hit_prob, seq_len) and bias towards same-route groupings, 3) cap token budget for mixed-route batches to avoid kernel switch.

leila: sketch of config I'm thinking (canary):
```yaml
batcher:
  formation:
    prefer_homogeneous_by: [route, model_variant]
  dynamic_token_budget:
    enabled: true
    default_target_p95_ms: 120
    per_route:
      search/gen-1:
        target_p95_ms: 130
        max_budget_tokens: 1500
        min_budget_tokens: 64
      chat/lowprio:
        target_p95_ms: 200
        max_budget_tokens: 4096
```

kevin: re kernel: we saw earlier that switching kernels (FP16->INT8 path) adds 3-6ms overhead per request when slices are mixed (due to setup + memory traffic). If we restrict mixing, we can avoid the pathological tail. Also KV cache thrash: we should increase per-slice KV warming for high-affinity routes.

sasha: can we do a quick canary? run on one dedicated worker pool with instrumentation: `./canary --route search/gen-1 --policy prefer_homogeneous_by=route --dyn_budget=true` and collect p95, kv_hit_rate, batch_size_dist.

perfbot: automated snapshot created: perf_snap/3098765432/initial (p95=412ms, kv_hit=68%, avg_batch_tokens=1420) :memo:

maria: I'll push a lightweight implementation: when queueing, compute group_score = route_weight*10 + kv_pref_score*5 - seq_len_penalty. Then greedily form batches only from top scoring group until either token_budget or homogeneous quota reached. Fallback to mixed batches if wait time > 40ms.

kevin: make sure to emit these metrics at route granularity: `route.p95_ms`, `route.kv_hit_rate`, `route.avg_batch_tokens`, `route.microbatch_wait_ms`, `route.kernel_switch_count`. We'll gate rollout on route.p95_ms decrease and no regression in avg_latency for other routes.

leila: also add a tester to replay prefix distributions; I have a replay corpus that reproduces kv churn. I'll run it against both current and canary batcher and post diffs.

sasha: one more risk: for big routes with high variance, per-route budget could starve smaller tenants. add cross-route fairness: if pool_util < 70% allow budget relaxation, else enforce strict per-route caps.

maria: noted. I'll implement the fairness gate and an emergency fallback to 'fast-path' routing if route.p95_ms spikes > 2x baseline for > 3min.

leila: perfect. action items: @maria implement canary change + metrics (ETA EOD), @kevin add kernel_switch_count metric and perf dashboard, @sasha run replay and initial canary traffic, I'll coordinate rollout and postmortem if needed. :chart_with_upwards_trend:

kevin: SGTM. one-off run command for QA: `./tools/run_canary.sh --pool=dedicated-a --route=search/gen-1 --duration=15m --metrics route.*`

perfbot: queued job 3098765432-canary-started. expected end 3098766338. results will be attached. :robot_face:

leila: thanks team — let's reconvene after the canary outputs. keeping eyes on kv_hit_rate and p95.
